Aditya —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a narrow redline that keeps the MSA intact and adds a pilot-specific Order Form clause (see MSA_Redline_TFC.docx). Summary of the proposed approach:

- Location: Add a short Rider/Order Form paragraph ("Pilot Exception") rather than changing core MSA term language. Keeps precedent.
- Scope: Applies only to the named Order Form and the Pilot Annex A; explicitly terminates on conversion to a committed term or expiry of the pilot.
- Notice: 30 days' written notice required to terminate the pilot under TFC.
- Exit fee: Customer may either (a) forfeit remaining prepaid pilot credits, or (b) pay an early-exit fee equal to one month of committed run rate — we suggest (a) for pilots less than 3 months, (b) for pilots >=3 months use fee (i.e., Tidewater fits case (b)).
- Transition obligations: Redwood will provide 30 days of transition support limited to data export and a single run of export scripts; we add a capped professional services rate for additional assistance.
- Auto-renew: Add explicit language that pilot exclusion modifies auto-renew only for the pilot period; after conversion, auto-renew and standard notice windows apply.

Risks / callouts:
- Operational: need to ensure an internal tag on the account so routing and billing do not auto-renew on pilot expiration. Product/ops must accept the tag.
- Precedent: this sets a pilot-exit precedent; recommend we limit to named pilots under $50k TCV or require manager approval for exceptions.

If you approve, I'll generate the Order Form paragraph and share with Procurement. Also added a short paragraph to preserve data-retention and security obligations post-termination.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Corporate Counsel — Redwood Inference
